trick: Add logging and run it before fixing (Cursor Debug Mode)
source_quote: "The agent then instruments your code with logging statements designed to test these hypotheses." ... "the agent removes all the instrumentation, leaving you with a clean, minimal change you can ship." (Cursor, Debug Mode)
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md.
behaviour_count: Runs that added log statements AND ran the program before their first non-logging source edit (events: Edit adding console.*/print, then a Bash run, then the fix), per side; plus log lines left in the final diff; plus the D2 (needs runtime observation) pass rate per side
habit_measure: Plain side: the same 'logged and ran before the fix' count, and plain runs that ran the program at all before their first edit
anchor: Told to log first, N of 18 watched it run before fixing and left L log lines behind; unprompted, M of 18 did

with.label: Cursor's loop as a prefix: hypotheses, temporary logs, reproduce, read, fix, remove the logs
with.prompt_prefix: Before you fix anything, come up with a few hypotheses about the cause and add temporary logging to the code to test them. Then run the steps that reproduce the bug and read what the logs show. Fix the bug based on what you saw, and remove all the logging you added before you finish.
